name: Rosalind Franklin
maker: Airbus Defence and Space for the European Space Agency
def: European ExoMars rover built to drill two metres below the surface of Oxia Planum in search of preserved organic biosignatures.
body: The Rosalind Franklin rover is completed flight hardware, assembled by Airbus in Stevenage and held in Turin after the 2022 launch was cancelled. It carries a two metre drill, the Mars Organic Molecule Analyser and a six wheel flexible chassis that can wheel walk out of soft ground, and NASA is supplying the launch, braking engines and radioisotope heater units. ESA now plans a 2028 launch on a Falcon Heavy with landing at Oxia Planum in 2030.
facts: Designed to drill two metres deep, far deeper than any previous Mars rover
Flight model is built and awaiting a 2028 launch
Named after the chemist whose X ray work underpinned DNA structure
specs: Six wheel flexible chassis with wheel walking locomotion
Solar arrays with radioisotope heater units for night survival
PanCam, ISEM, CLUPI, WISDOM radar, Ma_MISS borehole spectrometer, MOMA, MicrOmega, Raman spectrometer
Onboard autonomous navigation for long single sol traverses
